item.title: Setup Rails project on Codex AI
item.description: I’d like to try the new Codex AI and see if it’s suitable for our use cases. This is an example of how to set it up for a Rails project. Requirements Open AI Pro account Access to your Github Repositories on Data Controls - I suggest limit access to only the repositories you are working with Create a new environment Create a new environment Select the organisation and repository you want to set up Add any required environment variables for your dev environment; Exporting variables from the setup script does not work You must add environment variables using the UI, the script runs as a bash script and the variables are only available when it’s executing.

item.title: Aim to have a suite of tests that you can trust
item.description: It’s not just about Write tests, but writing tests that you can trust. Test the behaviour, not the implementation. Only test the things that could possibly break.

item.title: The Single Responsibility Principle is not about doing only one thing
item.description: Single Responsibility Principle is: Gather together the things that change for the same reasons. Separate those things that change for different reasons.” en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-responsibility_principle Tips for Software Engineers.

item.title: Fox Escape - Building a game with my kids using Claude Code
item.description: I’m starting to introduce code for my girls, they are 7 and 5 years old. One idea to create interest was brainstorming game ideas that they could play together and show their friends.

item.description: AI-Generated Workflow for a Project I keep updating it; that’s the current state as I write this. It’s too verbose now, but I kinda like this version.

item.title: MCP Warning
item.description: WARNING If you have the option to run in a Docker container, that’s safer. There are heaps of AI-generated servers, and they have full access to your machine and dot files.

item.title: Create meaningful connections with your peers
item.description: It’s easy to work with someone for months and still not really know them. You chat in meetings, reply to threads, and react to a meme or two. But it stays surface-level.

item.title: Implementing designs with Figma MCP Server
item.description: Set up Figma MCP by following their docs Framelink Figma getting started I gave it a try and got some good results from it. Set up the MCP with a token for your Figma, and you can then ask the AI to implement the design.

item.title: Running Obsidian on Supernote
item.description: I have a Supernote around and had some fun with it. It’s incredible to write down, and it has an excellent interface. You get addicted to it, but I stopped using it quite a while ago.

item.title: Self review
item.description: Own your contributions, self-review your code, read it pretending you are someone else, you will find gaps, fix them before sending to review. Related to Code review pyramid, and Tips for Software Engineers.
